profile_headline: Data Scientist | Craves to Learn | Loves to Solve | Lives to teach
post_content:
Companies not hiring freshers in DS - Why ? People curse companies for not
hiring freshers. Here is an an interesting perspective of small teams who are
kicking off AI - Investments are little and brittle mostly. Hence, there is no
space to train people to become 'real data scientists'. Education from most
institutes is too shallow. Most of aspirants are in 5-10 lpa and they spend
2-3 lakhs on institute which tell them your pay will be 2.5X after course.
After the course, aspirants expect min of 1.5X . For a company, it is
ridiculous to pay 10 lpa for 0 exp In case, he is open for training, the
company might ask to take a cut and prove and then talk 2X. I saw many people
who excelled after they took a pay cut and proved themselves. So, it all boils
down to economics rather than experience. This may not be true in MNC's which
are cash rich. I align with pain of many aspirants like you. But the same is
the pain for startups (includes small AI teams in huge MNC's) who hire data
scientists and couldn't deliver results and are under heavy pressure. PS :
This post isn't blaming some one on higher pay demands . It's a reality - lot
of people have to wake up to - before investing 2-3 lakhs in expectation of
2x-3x hikes. hashtag#ai hashtag#datascience hashtag#machinelearning
hashtag#endtoendDS

Practical real world example of Selection - Sampling bias Statistician goes
into class taking data science using python and asks 3 question to publish
findings Q. 1) How many of you are using Python? A. 1) All of them raises
hands. Q. 2) How many of you are using R? A. 2) All hands down. Q. 3) How many
of you using SAS? A. 3) All hands down Finally publishes the finding. Python -
100%, R - 0%, SAS - 0% Let us leave aside the distribution or test used. :)
How to mitigate such bias is simple - Random Sample where each group under
survey has equal chance of being chosen If you still did not get why I wrote -
Search LinkedIn you might find the reason :) . Sometimes outcome might be
obvious to many but by going into survey with obvious answer is Confirmation
bias Read my article in first comment on tools above hashtag#datascience
hashtag#datacollection hashtag#statistics
